"Upgrade Flow: rollout and execution"

Stage 4 of the Upgrade Flow — plan how many appliances go down per round, save the rollout as scheduled tasks once the change is approved, and follow execution appliance by appliance.

👤 ForAdministratorOperator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage backups.create backups.restore
📍 WhereAutomation → Upgrade Flow, card 4 (URL /web/upgrade-flow/), and the execution page /web/upgrade-flow/change/<id>

What is it?#

Once the change request for a window exists, card 4 — Scheduled rollout decides how many of its appliances go down at a time. Each round becomes a real one-shot task on Automations (and on the Calendar) bound to the change, and is re-checked against the change's approval and window when it fires. The Execution page shows per-appliance progress while the rounds run.

What does it do?#

  • Splits the change's appliances into rounds of at most N appliances, a fixed number of minutes apart, starting at the window start.
  • Before approval, saves the plan on the change without creating any task. When the change is approved, the plan is turned into scheduled tasks automatically.
  • After approval, creates or updates the scheduled tasks directly.
  • Shows the saved rounds (start time, appliances, state).
  • On the execution page, polls progress every 5 seconds and offers Start now inside an approved window.

What execution does today#

⚠️Warning — No firmware is flashed by the scheduled upgrade

The automated firmware-upgrade executor is a guarded placeholder in this release. When a round fires inside its window, every appliance is graded failed with the summary "Firmware upgrade for <appliance> is not executed by the headless service layer (no upgrade runbook); no firmware was flashed.", and the change request then closes as failed. Use the rollout to plan and document the window; perform the flash per appliance from the Firmware page, which requires its own approved, open change request.

Multi-round rollouts#

All rounds of a rollout are bound to the same change request. A round that succeeds and is not the last leaves the change in progress for the next round; only the last round closes it, as completed when it succeeded. A round that fails closes the change as failed at once, so the remaining rounds are refused at fire time ("change request: change request is failed") instead of flashing on.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: a rollout split into rounds is no longer closed by its first round, and the Schedule button on the change request now honours the rollout plan saved on the change.

The execution page follows the task bound to the change (the first round), so appliances of later rounds show not_run there once round 1 is over; follow later rounds on Automations. To follow each group on its own execution page, use waves: one change request per group.

Requirements#

  • A change raised by the flow (card 4 appears only while stage 3 shows a change).
  • To save a plan: the change is not completed, failed or cancelled, it has a window start, and its type has an automated executor (the upgrade type does).
  • To create scheduled tasks: additionally, the change is approved (or already scheduled).
  • To start execution: the change is approved, its external approval (if any) is granted, the current time is inside the window, and the change has a bound scheduled task.

Permissions#

Action Required permission
Card 4: Save rollout plan / Save as scheduled task users.manage
Open the execution page and its live progress backups.create or backups.restore
Start now on the execution page users.manage

Users without users.manage do not see card 4; on the execution page the Start now button is still drawn, but pressing it returns 403. The Open change links lead to the change's own page, which also requires users.manage.

How to use#

Plan the rollout (card 4)#

  1. Raise the change in stage 2; the flow reloads with stage 3 and card 4.
  2. Read the coverage line: "This change covers N appliance(s)."
  3. Set Appliances per round (1 to the number of appliances) and Minutes between rounds (1–1440). The round count updates as you type ("3 rounds × 5"). For a one-appliance change both fields are read-only.
  4. Click the save button: - Save rollout plan — shown while the change is not yet approved. An info box says "Not scheduled yet: approve the change request before scheduling it" and that the rounds are created the moment the change is approved. - Save as scheduled task — shown once the change is approved or scheduled.
  5. If the button is disabled, the warning "Nothing can be planned yet: …" names the reason (for example set a maintenance-window start first); set the window from the action bar in stage 3.

After saving as scheduled tasks, the card shows Saved as scheduled task #id, links to Automations and Calendar (or "(the calendar is switched off for your user)"), and a table of rounds: Round, Starts, Appliances, State (scheduled, disabled or the last run status).

ℹ️Note — Two scheduling controls

The Schedule/Re-schedule button in the stage 3 action bar (and on the change request's own page) reads the rollout plan saved on the change — its appliances per round and minutes between rounds — and schedules those rounds. Without a saved plan it schedules the whole change as one round. Card 4's button saves and schedules the plan in one step.

Follow execution#

  1. Open the execution page: from Batched rollouts on the Upgrade Flow page, click a wave k/N button; or browse to /web/upgrade-flow/change/<id>.
  2. Read the progress bar (percentage of appliances that reported ok or failed) and the line "D of T appliance(s) reported — O ok, F failed." followed by "Run #id: status".
  3. The Per appliance table lists every appliance of the change with State, Result and Took (ms).
  4. In Start execution, click Start now to bring the scheduled fire forward. The scheduler picks it up within a minute.
State Meaning
pending Not reached yet
running Being processed
ok / failed Outcome recorded for this appliance
interrupted The run ended while this appliance was still running (worker stopped) — no outcome was measured
not_run The run finished without ever reaching this appliance

An amber box "No pre-upgrade baseline for: …" lists appliances of the change without a bound pre-upgrade run.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Appliances per round Maximum appliances per round; clamped to the change's appliance count Yes 5
Minutes between rounds Gap between round starts (default 60) No 45

Example#

🧪Example — Ten appliances, approved change, window 22:00–02:00

Appliances per round = 4, Minutes between rounds = 60 → three rounds starting 22:00, 23:00 and 00:00 (4, 4 and 2 appliances). Save as scheduled task flashes "The task “CR #12: … - round 1/3” has been added to Scheduled Actions and is on the calendar." and "It runs in 3 rounds of at most 4 appliance(s), 60 minute(s) apart — the first at <window start in the console timezone>."

Result#

  • Plan saved (not approved): the plan is stored on the change and a rollout planned event is added to its timeline; the status does not change. Flash: "Rollout plan saved on this change: N round(s) of at most S appliance(s), G minute(s) apart. Nothing is in Automations or on the calendar yet — the rounds are created the moment this change is approved." Audit entry upgrade_flow.plan.
  • On approval: the saved plan becomes scheduled tasks through the same call as Save as scheduled task. If that fails, the plan stays on the change.
  • Scheduled: one one-shot task per round on Automations (named CR #<id>: <title> - round k/N when there are several), all bound to the change; the change moves to scheduled. Re-saving replaces the previous extra rounds. Audit entry upgrade_flow.schedule.
  • Start now: the bound task's next run is set to now and the task is enabled; audit entry upgrade_flow.start_now. Flash: "Execution requested. The scheduler picks it up within a minute and this page shows each appliance as it is reached."
  • At fire time the change moves to in progress. The last round closes it as completed if every appliance succeeded; any round that fails closes it as failed and the remaining rounds do not run.

Troubleshooting#

"Set how many appliances go in each round. Nothing was scheduled."#

Possible causes - Appliances per round was empty or 0.

Solution 1. Enter a number from 1 to the appliance count and save again.

Verification - The save flash appears.

"… is N rounds; at most 24 are scheduled at once."#

Possible causes - The appliance count divided by Appliances per round exceeds 24.

Solution 1. Raise Appliances per round. Nothing was scheduled.

Verification - The rounds table lists at most 24 rounds.

"N rounds G minute(s) apart would start the last one at …, after this change's window closes at …"#

Possible causes - The last round would start after the window end and would be refused at fire time.

Solution 1. Widen the window, raise the appliances per round, or shorten the gap.

Verification - The save succeeds and the last round's Starts is inside the window.

"Nothing can be planned yet: set a maintenance-window start first"#

Possible causes - The change has no window start.

Solution 1. Use Edit in the stage 3 action bar to set the window, then save the plan.

Verification - The save button is enabled.

"Round k of this change is running right now. Re-planning would delete the record of a fire that is in progress. Nothing was changed."#

Possible causes - A round of this change is executing.

Solution 1. Wait for the round to finish, then re-plan.

Verification - The rounds table shows a final state for every round.

"Not started — before the maintenance window. The maintenance window is the authorization; this button does not replace it."#

The reason after Not started — can also be after the maintenance window, change request is not approved, no maintenance window, or an external approval reason.

Possible causes - The change is not approved, the external approval is missing, or the current time is outside the window.

Solution 1. Approve the change (and obtain the external approval if the mode is External), or wait for the window to open.

Verification - The execution page shows Start now instead of "Not startable right now: …".

"This change has no bound action yet — schedule it first."#

Possible causes - The change was approved but never scheduled.

Solution 1. Save the rollout in card 4 (or use Schedule on the change), then return.

Verification - The execution page shows Start now.

"The bound action is already running."#

Possible causes - The scheduled task is already executing.

Solution 1. Watch the progress table; no action is needed.

Verification - The progress bar advances.

"That change request is not one this flow can schedule — it does not exist, or it is not visible to you. Nothing was scheduled."#

Possible causes - The change was deleted, or names only appliances outside your ADOM or visibility.

Solution 1. Open the change from Change Requests in the correct ADOM.

Verification - Card 4 appears for the change.

Every appliance shows failed with "no firmware was flashed"#

Possible causes - Expected in this release; see What execution does today.

Solution 1. Flash each appliance from the Firmware page during the window.

Verification - The appliance's firmware version shows the new release after rediscovery.

Advanced#

Advanced Round arithmetic

Round k starts at window start + (k − 1) × gap. Appliances are split in the order stored on the change. A round size that covers every appliance produces a single task without round numbering. The plan is re-validated with the same rules when the change is approved.

Advanced Authorization at fire time

Each round task carries the change reference. When it fires, the executor re-checks that the change is approved/scheduled/in progress, that any external approval is granted and that the current time is inside the window; otherwise the fire is skipped. Start now never bypasses this check.

Advanced Polling

The execution page polls /web/upgrade-flow/change/<id>/progress.json every 5 seconds and stops once the run is no longer running. A failed poll leaves the last state on screen.
